title: Hearty Polish Pork Hash
description: A winey, crumbly, kid-friendly Polish dish featuring allspice berries, this paleo-friendly hash is perfect for a weeknight dinner. It is made with ground pork, rice, and spices, cooked to perfection on a tava griddle.
instructions: Heat a tava griddle over medium heat and add a tablespoon of oil to the surface.
Add the chopped onion to the griddle and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic to the griddle and cook for an additional minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the ground pork to the griddle, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks, until it is no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the cooked rice, allspice berries, salt, and black pepper to the griddle, stirring to combine with the pork mixture.
If using red wine, add it to the griddle and stir to combine, cooking for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the liquid has been absorbed.
Use a spatula to shape the hash into a flat, round shape, and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the bottom is crispy and golden brown.
Flip the hash over and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the other side is also crispy and golden brown.
Remove the hash from the griddle and serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
